# From linked data to research-ready data {#sec-pipeline} ::: {.cell} ::: The linked table from the linkage stage (@sec-sources-linkage) is accurate to its sources, but not yet easy to analyse. The same make is spelt dozens of ways, attributes are missing for many vehicles, and some DVLA records belong to another vehicle. The pipeline, [MOT-pipline](https://github.com/CARS-Project/MOT-pipline), cleans and enhances the table and produces the published outputs. This chapter summarises what it does; the full method, with every rule and count, is in the pipeline's [Methodology](../reports/methodology.md), included as an appendix. ## Principles Four principles run through the pipeline, and they shape how the data should be used: 1. **Supplied values are never overwritten.** Cleaned, harmonised or filled values go in new columns next to the originals. `fuel_DVSA` is the fuel as DVSA supplied it; `fuel` is the harmonised fuel. 2. **Every inferred value records its source.** Columns ending `_src`, `_method` and `_check` say how each value was reached, so you can always separate what was recorded from what was inferred. 3. **Weak evidence is flagged, not acted on.** A value is changed only when the vehicle's own records disagree and a second source settles it. 4. **Results are reproducible.** Every step is a rule (no language model or random element is used), and rebuilding from the same input gives the same output. ## The stages ```{mermaid} flowchart TD A[Linked and annualised
vehicle table] --> B[1. Core table
scope, dates, yearly status] B --> C[2. Make and model
matched to DfT names] T[DfT vehicle licensing
statistics] --> C A --> M[3a. DVSA-DVLA
record check] C --> F[3b. Fuel and engine checks] M --> F F --> D[3c. Fill gaps from
similar vehicles] D --> E[4. Vehicle table
vehicles_enhanced.parquet] E --> G[Churn tables] E --> H[Mileage and fleet
profile tables] E --> I[Quality reports] ``` ### 1. Core table: which vehicles, and their dates The input holds 138,238,617 vehicles, many of which left the roads long before 2005. The pipeline keeps every vehicle with evidence that it existed from 2005 onwards: a recorded mileage or postcode area in any year, a birth date from 2005, or DVLA activity (tax, V5C, MOT expiry or first registration) since 2005. That leaves **93,352,241 vehicles**. The `scope_*` columns record which evidence each vehicle has. It also sets each vehicle's `birth_date` (the earliest of its first-use, registration and manufacture dates) and `first_use_date`, and fills the blank years of `pca_YYYY` with the statuses `unborn`, `unknown` and `dead` (@sec-lifecycle). ### 2. Make and model DVSA records make and model as free text, entered at the test station. "FORD FIESTA ZETEC CLIMATE", "Fiesta" and "MOMDEO" all occur. The pipeline matches each distinct make and model to the names DfT uses in its vehicle licensing statistics, through a sequence of rules (exact match, generic name, prefix, words, spelling fixes) that each record how they matched: | Column | Example | |---|---| | `make_final` | `FORD` | | `model_final` | `FIESTA` (DfT's *generic model*) | | `derivative_final` | `ZETEC CLIMATE`: the rest of the model text | | `dft_genmodel` | `FORD FIESTA`, for joining to DfT tables | | `make_method`, `model_method`, `model_confidence` | How the match was made, and how sure it is | Using DfT's names means CARS results can be joined to and compared with the official statistics. The DfT scheme is sometimes coarser than a buyer would use (DfT's DISCOVERY includes the Discovery Sport), and the derivative keeps the detail. The match also gives each vehicle a DfT `body_type` (@sec-vehicle-types). ### 3. Checking and harmonising attributes Eight attributes are *harmonised*: given one best value per vehicle from the DVSA record, the DVLA record and, where both are missing, similar vehicles. They are `fuel`, `engine_cc`, `co2`, `euro_status`, `type_approval`, `revenue_weight`, `wheelplan` and `test_class`. - **Is the DVLA record the same vehicle?** The make, year and engine size of the DVSA and DVLA records are compared. Where two or more disagree (`dvla_match = 'different'`), the DVLA record is taken to describe another vehicle and none of its values is used. - **Fuel** is taken from the records and never filled from other vehicles. DVLA's fuel is used where DVSA says "Other", or where DVSA says Electric for a vehicle that has an engine. Plug-in hybrids are identified from DfT's records for the model (@sec-fuels-emissions). `fuel_check` compares each vehicle's fuel with others of its make and model, and flags rare fuels. - **Engine size** is 0 for electric vehicles. - **Gaps** in the other attributes are filled with the most common value among vehicles of the same make, model, birth year and fuel (and engine size where known). Values are never borrowed across fuels. - **Euro status** that is still missing is assumed from the standard compulsory when the vehicle was made (@sec-fuels-emissions). ::: {#tbl-harmonised .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='Where the harmonised attributes come from: share of vehicles in the vehicle table.'} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Attribute | Recorded| Rule (no engine, DfT, model check, Euro schedule)| From similar vehicles| Missing| |:--------------|--------:|-------------------------------------------------:|---------------------:|-------:| |fuel | 98.8%| 1.2%| 0.0%| 0.0%| |engine_cc | 93.7%| 2.9%| 2.5%| 0.9%| |revenue_weight | 30.4%| 0.0%| 39.3%| 30.2%| |co2 | 54.0%| 0.0%| 20.0%| 26.0%| |euro_status | 14.5%| 55.2%| 21.5%| 8.8%| |type_approval | 59.0%| 0.0%| 22.3%| 18.6%| |wheelplan | 76.8%| 0.0%| 22.6%| 0.5%| |test_class | 79.3%| 0.0%| 14.8%| 5.9%| ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip title="Recorded values only"} To check that a result does not depend on filled values, repeat it using only recorded ones: filter on `co2_src = 'dvla'`, `euro_status_src = 'dvla'`, `engine_cc_src IN ('dvsa', 'dvla')` and so on, or use the supplied columns (`co2Emissions_DVLA`, `euroStatus_DVLA`). @sec-examples-code has an example. ::: ### 4. Number plates and derived fields The registration number is decoded to its format, issue period and issuing office, and flagged where it does not match the vehicle's age (@sec-number-plates). Simplified groupings such as `fuel_simple` and `euro_standard` are added. ### Outputs The result is the vehicle table, `vehicles_enhanced.parquet`, with its data dictionary (@sec-vehicle-table). From it the pipeline builds the aggregate tables (@sec-aggregate-tables) and a set of reports that document them, included in this book as appendices. ## Validation The pipeline has unit tests for every rule, a set of cross-checks run on every build that compare published numbers that must agree, comparisons with DfT's statistics (@sec-data-quality), and a record of an end-to-end audit. See the [MOT-pipline repository](https://github.com/CARS-Project/MOT-pipline) for details.
